fonti.nota: Art. 13 (rates and reductions) in force since 1 January 2018; art. 5 (exemptions). Consolidated text last updated 17/05/2025.

fonti.titolo: Law 5162/2024, art. 24 (amending art. 53 of Law 4389/2016) - Government Gazette ΦΕΚ Α' 198/05.12.2024
fonti.nota: Official copy of the Government Gazette served by search.et.gr (National Printing House). Applies from tax year 2025 (art. 136 par. 7).

fonti.titolo: Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) - climate resilience fee page
fonti.nota: Blocks automated reading (403): checked by hand each quarter.

note: The fee is charged per room or apartment per night, not per person: two people sharing a room pay one fee.
April to October is the high-season rate; November to March the low-season rate. For stays across two months with different rates, the receipt is issued per month.

The same national rate applies everywhere in Greece. Cruise passengers pay a separate cruise fee (not covered here).
esenzioni: Accommodation provided free of charge (the fee is not imposed)

categorie.label: Hotels, holiday villages, guesthouses and other paid accommodation

tariffe.nota: Rate in Law 6802 art. 34 once Decision 11263 expires on 31/12/2026, unless a new decision changes it.

fonti.titolo: Presidential Decision No. 11263, Official Gazette (Resmî Gazete) No. 33240, 1 May 2026: accommodation tax rate set at 1% until 31/12/2026
Revenue Administration (GİB) - accommodation tax return guide: rate 2%, base = invoice amount excluding VAT

note: The accommodation tax (konaklama vergisi) is a percentage of the price excluding VAT of the overnight stay and of the other services sold together with it at the property (food, drinks, activities, entertainment, pool, spa and similar), so with board or all-inclusive the base is wider than the room alone.
From 1 May 2026 to 31 December 2026 the rate is 1% (Presidential Decision 11263). Before that it was 2%, the rate in the law.
If you booked a package, check with your tour operator or hotel whether the tax is already included.
The tax is national: the same rate applies in Istanbul, Antalya, Bodrum, Dalaman, Fethiye, Marmaris and Cappadocia.

From 1 May 2026 to 31 December 2026 the rate is 1% (Presidential Decision 11263). Before that it was 2%, the rate in the law.
If you booked a package, check with your tour operator or hotel whether the tax is already included.

destinazioni.name: Amsterdam
destinazioni.official_name: Tourist tax (toeristenbelasting)
destinazioni.etichetta_prezzo: Overnight price per night, excluding VAT and breakfast (all rooms booked)

categorie.label: Hotels, holiday rentals, B&Bs, campsites and all other paid overnight stays

destinazioni.chi_riscuote: The accommodation provider is liable for the tax and may pass it on to the guest.

fonti.titolo: Verordening Toeristenbelasting 2024 (Amsterdam tourist tax ordinance), official regulations repository CVDR703815 - art. 4 (base) and art. 5 (12.5%)
fonti.nota: Still the version in force in the national CVDR register on the check date (no later version).

fonti.titolo: City of Amsterdam - tourist tax page
fonti.nota: Blocks automated reading: checked by hand.

note: 12.5% of the price of the overnight stay, excluding VAT and excluding the tourist tax itself. Charges closely linked to the stay (cleaning, bed linen, towels) count even if invoiced separately; breakfast, food and drinks do not.
There is no age exemption and no cap on the number of nights.
Amsterdam also has a separate day-tourist tax (dagtoeristenbelasting), not covered here.
esenzioni: People staying in recognised care institutions
Government-arranged shelter for refugees and homeless people

Senate Department for Finance - City Tax FAQ: main changes to the Overnight Stay Tax Act 2024-2026 (7.5% from 1 January 2025, 21-day rule abolished)
Berlin Service Portal - Übernachtungsteuer: 7.5% of the net price of the overnight stay, without extras such as breakfast

note: 7.5% of the price of the overnight stay, excluding VAT and excluding other services such as breakfast.
Business trips are taxed too. The old rule that ended the tax after 21 nights was abolished from 2025; stays offered for less than six months are covered.
There is no age exemption in the law.

destinazioni.name: Vienna
destinazioni.official_name: Ortstaxe (local accommodation tax)
destinazioni.etichetta_prezzo: Accommodation price per night, excluding VAT and breakfast (all rooms booked)

tariffe.nota: 3.2% after a flat 11% deduction from the price

destinazioni.chi_riscuote: The accommodation owner, who collects it and pays it to the City of Vienna by the 15th of the following month.

fonti.titolo: City of Vienna - Ortstaxe (rates until 30 June 2026, from 1 July 2026 and from 1 July 2027; exemptions)

note: From 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027: 5% of the price of the stay, excluding VAT and breakfast.
Until 30 June 2026 it was 3.2% after a flat 11% deduction; from 1 July 2027 it will be 8%.
The City of Vienna also publishes an official online Ortstaxe calculator for hosts.
People who stay more than 3 months without interruption in the accommodation are exempt: the calculator shows no tax for such stays.

destinazioni.name: Prague

categorie.label: Hotels, apartments, hostels and all paid stays

destinazioni.chi_riscuote: The accommodation provider, who pays it to the City or the city district.

fonti.titolo: Prague ordinance No. 19/2021 amending ordinance 18/2019 (rate 21 CZK -> 50 CZK; stays up to 60 consecutive days), Collection of Legal Regulations of Local Authorities
Prague ordinance No. 18/2019 on the local fee for stay (original text: per person per day except the day of arrival)
Act No. 565/1990 on local fees, current version (§3b exemptions incl. persons under 18; §3c base = days of stay except arrival day), e-Sbírka

note: 50 CZK per person for each day of the stay except the day of arrival (so one fee per night).

Only paid stays lasting at most 60 consecutive calendar days with the same provider are covered. The arrival day counts as a day of the stay, so a stay of 60 nights or more (61+ calendar days) is outside the fee.
Under-18s are exempt by national law.
Other exemptions in national law include blind and severely disabled people (ZTP/P) with a companion, and people hospitalised in the city.
esenzioni: Persons under 18
Blind people, ZTP/P card holders and their companion
Hospitalised patients (except spa care)
Seasonal workers
Some social and emergency stays

fonti.titolo: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Taxation - accommodation tax FAQ (current rates, planned April 2027 change, children)
